script.opening: (Confident, gym clothes on, slightly sheepish under the bravado.) "Doc, I'm just constantly knackered — no energy, my sex drive's dropped, my gym gains have stalled. My mate at the gym reckons it's low testosterone, and I've seen loads online about it. Can you just test it and give me a testosterone boost? Or honestly, where's the harm in just trying some?"

facts.text: "A few months. More just flat and drained" — about 4 months. Not sleepy in the day, more no energy.
"I don't sleep brilliantly, if I'm honest. I don't know about snoring." Bed at 1 am after gaming; up at 6 for the gym. Lives alone.
"Bit flat, yeah. Nothing massive." If asked directly: no thoughts of self-harm. Stressed about a job change and a recent break-up.
"I train most days. I push it hard" — 6–7 days a week, no rest days, plus 5 km runs. Eating "clean", cutting carbs to get lean; lost 4 kg in 2 months. Pre-workout supplements with lots of caffeine.
"Mainly just not in the mood." Morning erections still present. No breast swelling, no testicular problems.
"I've looked into it. That's partly why I'm asking you. I'd rather do it properly." Has bought a "natural test booster" online; hasn't injected anything. Gym mate has offered him some.
No regular medicines, no allergies. No past illnesses. Drinks 15–20 units at weekends. Non-smoker. Planning children "one day" with a future partner.
Estate agent; recently changed jobs; long hours.

Keen on the quick fix but genuinely wants to do it properly. Challenges: "But what if it is low T?" and "And the harm in just trying some?" Taken aback by fertility risk: "I didn't know about the fertility thing." Agrees to ease off training. If lectured or mocked, becomes defensive and says he'll "just get it online".

ice.ideas: "It's low testosterone — a boost will fix it."
ice.concerns: HIDDEN AGENDA — doing "everything right" and going backwards; body image; a recent break-up and work stress he hasn't linked to the tiredness; tempted by a friend's offer of steroids.

cues: "Where's the harm in just trying some?" — the risk conversation.
"I'd rather do it properly." — invites asking about gym products.
"Going backwards." — overtraining and under-eating to explore.

checkpoints.text: Resists the "just test it and give me testosterone" request and works up the FATIGUE structurally — screening sleep/OSA (NICE NG202), mood/depression with a self-harm question (NICE NG222), stress, diet, overtraining, alcohol/drugs, anaemia, thyroid, diabetes — as for any TATT

Assesses for genuine HYPOGONADISM symptoms and, IF indicated, tests CORRECTLY per BSSM 2023 — two MORNING total testosterone samples (7–11am, ideally fasting) on separate occasions, with LH, FSH, SHBG ± free testosterone, prolactin and FBC — not a single random level
BUSTS THE MYTH that testosterone is a fatigue/energy/performance tonic, and that "where’s the harm in trying" is safe — it is not for men with normal levels

Spells out the HARMS of inappropriate testosterone/anabolic steroids — suppression of endogenous production, INFERTILITY and testicular atrophy, polycythaemia/thrombosis risk, gynaecomastia, mood/cardiovascular effects, unregulated products — especially the fertility risk

Asks NON-JUDGEMENTALLY about current/considered gym/online testosterone, anabolic steroid or "booster"/SARM use — recognising it may be causing his symptoms and matters for safe management/harm reduction (needle and syringe programme per NICE PH52 if he injects)
Takes the fatigue and low libido seriously, reads the body-image/online influence, and educates honestly WITHOUT being dismissive or preachy — not simply refusing or simply complying
Manages the ACTUAL cause found, and only considers testosterone replacement for genuine, correctly-confirmed hypogonadism (usually with specialist/endocrine input)

Safety-nets and follows up: appropriate fatigue investigations and review, correct testosterone testing only if indicated, harm-reduction/steroid-cessation support if relevant, treatment of the real cause, and review — honest education, not handing over testosterone

worked.txt: "Being constantly knackered with a low sex drive is genuinely worth sorting — so I do want to help. But I’d be doing you a disservice if I just tested testosterone and handed you a boost, because in a young man that’s actually an uncommon cause, and there are several more likely ones we’d miss."

"Let me ask properly: how’s your sleep — snoring, waking unrefreshed? Your mood and stress — and if you’ve been feeling flat, any thoughts of harming yourself? Drinking, diet, how hard you’re training and recovering? … I’ll also do bloods — thyroid, blood count, sugar — because these are the usual culprits for this kind of tiredness."

"If your symptoms point to genuinely low testosterone, we test it properly — two morning samples between 7 and 11, ideally before eating, on different days, plus some related hormones — not a random one-off, because levels swing about and a single low reading can mislead."
"Here’s the honest bit: testosterone isn’t an energy tonic. If your level is normal, taking it won’t fix the tiredness — and ‘no harm in trying’ really isn’t true here."

"Taking testosterone or gym steroids when you don’t need them shuts down your own production — which can make you INFERTILE and shrink the testicles — thickens the blood and raises clot and stroke risk, and the gym/online stuff is unregulated. The fertility one catches a lot of young men out."

"Can I ask without any judgement — are you taking, or thinking about, any gym or online testosterone, steroids or boosters? … That’s really useful to know, because it can actually cause exactly these symptoms, and I can help you do this safely. Let’s find and fix the real reason you’re so tired."

f.learning: Fatigue with low libido in a young man has many causes, and testosterone deficiency is an uncommon and heavily over-attributed one — so resist the "just test it and give me a T boost" request (driven by online "low-T" content and gym culture) and work the fatigue up structurally, screening sleep/insomnia/OSA (NICE NG202), mood/depression with a direct self-harm question (NICE NG222) and stress, diet, overtraining/under-recovery, alcohol/drugs, anaemia, thyroid disease and diabetes, as for any "tired all the time" presentation. If symptoms genuinely suggest HYPOGONADISM (low libido, erectile dysfunction, reduced morning erections, low energy/mood, reduced muscle mass, gynaecomastia, small testes), confirm it CORRECTLY (BSSM guideline, Hackett et al 2023): two MORNING (7–11am, ideally fasting) total testosterone samples on separate occasions (levels vary and fall with acute illness and through the day), with LH, FSH, SHBG (± calculated free testosterone), prolactin and FBC — not a single random level — with a confirmed low result needing explanation (primary vs secondary) and usually specialist/endocrine input. Crucially, bust the MYTH that testosterone is a fatigue/energy/performance tonic and that "where’s the harm in trying" is safe: giving testosterone to a man with normal levels (or self-sourced anabolic steroids) is harmful, suppressing endogenous testosterone and sperm production to cause INFERTILITY (the most underestimated harm in young men) and testicular atrophy, plus polycythaemia (thrombosis/stroke risk), gynaecomastia, mood/cardiovascular effects, with unregulated, potentially contaminated gym/online products. Ask NON-JUDGEMENTALLY about current/considered gym or online testosterone, anabolic steroid, "booster" or SARM use, as it is common, may itself be causing his symptoms (post-cycle hypogonadism), and matters for safe management and harm reduction (needle and syringe programmes include people who inject image- and performance-enhancing drugs — NICE PH52, 2014). Take the fatigue and low libido seriously, educate honestly without being dismissive or preachy, treat the actual cause, and reserve testosterone replacement for genuine, correctly-confirmed hypogonadism with specialist input.

knowledge.guideline: [1] BSSM guideline on adult testosterone deficiency (Hackett et al., World J Mens Health 2023) · [2] NICE NG202 Obstructive sleep apnoea hypopnoea syndrome and obesity hypoventilation syndrome in over 16s (2021) · [3] NICE NG222 Depression in adults (2022, updated December 2025) · [4] NICE PH52 Needle and syringe programmes (2014)
knowledge.summary: Tiredness with low libido in a fit 32-year-old is usually sleep, mood, stress, alcohol, overtraining or a common blood abnormality. Work it up like any tiredness. Test testosterone only when symptoms suggest it, and then properly. Be clear that testosterone is not a tonic and can cause infertility.

points.t: Screen sleep quantity and quality (snoring, witnessed apnoeas, daytime sleepiness: NICE NG202 [2] suggests Epworth or STOP-Bang), mood and anhedonia (NICE NG222 [3]), stress, alcohol and drugs, diet, and training load with inadequate recovery. First-line bloods: FBC, ferritin, TSH, HbA1c, renal and liver function, with others guided by history.

Test if symptoms suggest deficiency: reduced libido, erectile dysfunction, fewer morning erections, reduced muscle bulk, gynaecomastia, or small testes. Low libido with tiredness alone is non-specific.

BSSM 2023 [1]: diagnosis needs consistent symptoms plus two morning total testosterone samples (7–11am, ideally fasting) on separate occasions, with LH and FSH to separate primary from secondary causes, and SHBG, prolactin and FBC. Acute illness lowers testosterone, so avoid testing when unwell.
In men with normal levels, testosterone does not treat tiredness. BSSM [1] reserves treatment for confirmed deficiency with symptoms, and it is not for men who want to preserve fertility.

points.h: Harms of testosterone and anabolic steroids
points.t: Exogenous androgens suppress LH and FSH, so the testes make less testosterone and fewer sperm: infertility and testicular shrinkage, which may be slow to recover. Also raised haematocrit (BSSM [1] monitoring threshold 54%), acne, gynaecomastia, mood change, adverse lipids and cardiovascular risk. Gym or online products are unregulated and may be contaminated.

Ask directly and without judgement about testosterone, anabolic steroids, SARMs or “boosters”. Stopping after a cycle can itself cause low mood, low libido and tiredness. NICE PH52 [4] includes people who inject image- and performance-enhancing drugs in needle and syringe programmes.

If two morning levels are low with symptoms, look for the cause (including prolactin and pituitary causes when LH is low or normal) and involve endocrinology or a specialist men’s health service before treatment.

Sleep problems, depression, overtraining, alcohol, anaemia, thyroid, diabetes, androgen use or withdrawal, true hypogonadism.
Asked about specific hypogonadism features, low mood and self-harm; recognised anabolic steroid use as a cause and a risk.
Explained that low testosterone is an unlikely cause and that the work-up comes first.
After open exploration, used closed questions with clear signposting to confirm specific details.
Used information already available in the notes/referral; did not re-ask what was already documented or said.

dg.t: Finishes data gathering in good time
dg.d: History, ICE, psychosocial context and red-flag screen completed by ~6–7 minutes, leaving time for explanation and a shared plan.

Review in two weeks with results; mood safety-net; teach-back.

Idea (low testosterone), concern (going backwards despite effort), expectation (a test and a prescription).
Warm, non-judgmental tone; put the patient at ease and showed respect for their perspective.
Opened broadly and let the patient tell their story before narrowing down.
When a cue was offered, stopped and explored the specific concern rather than reassuring superficially and moving on.
Active listening throughout — reflecting, pausing, not interrupting — interested in the patient as a person.

Checked understanding, offered written/follow-up support, asked if anything else was on their mind, agreed next steps.

model.text: Hello Ryan, it’s Dr Okafor. Thanks for joining the video call. What’s been going on?

I’m just constantly knackered. No energy, my sex drive’s dropped and my gym gains have stalled. My mate reckons it’s low testosterone, and I’ve seen loads online. Can you test it and give me a boost? Or honestly, where’s the harm in just trying some?

Being tired all the time with a low sex drive is worth getting to the bottom of, so I’m glad you’ve come. I’d like to understand the tiredness properly first, then we’ll talk about testosterone, including whether and how to test it. Does that sound fair?
model.why: Takes the symptom seriously and sets an agenda without refusing outright

model.text: Fair enough.
How long has it been going on, and is it sleepiness, like nodding off, or more a lack of energy and motivation?
A few months. More just flat and drained.
How are you sleeping? Does anyone say you snore or stop breathing at night, and do you wake refreshed?
I don’t sleep brilliantly, if I’m honest. I don’t know about snoring.
And how’s your mood — are you still enjoying things, or has that gone flat too? Any stress at work or at home?
Bit flat, yeah. Nothing massive.
How much are you training at the moment, and how much rest are you getting between sessions? And how’s your eating and drinking?
I train most days. I push it hard.
When you say your sex drive has dropped, have you noticed any change in erections, including morning erections, or any change in your chest or testicles?
model.why: Looks for specific features of hypogonadism

model.text: Mainly just not in the mood.
I’m going to ask this without any judgement, because a lot of men who train seriously do it. Are you taking, or have you taken, any testosterone, steroids, SARMs or boosters from the gym or online?
I’ve looked into it. That’s partly why I’m asking you. I’d rather do it properly.
I really appreciate you telling me, and asking first is the sensible thing to do.
What do you think is going on, and what worries you most?
I think it’s low T. What bugs me is I’m doing everything right in the gym and going backwards.
So you’re putting the work in and not getting the results, and feeling rubbish with it. And you were hoping for a test and a prescription today?
model.why: Reflects the frustration and body-image element

model.text: Pretty much.

Here’s what I think. In a fit man your age, low testosterone is an uncommon cause of this. Poor sleep, low mood, training hard without enough recovery, and things like low iron or thyroid problems are much more common, and you’ve mentioned a few already.
But what if it is low T?

Then we test it properly: two blood samples in the morning, between 7 and 11, on different days, with some related hormones. A single random test can be misleading because levels vary through the day and drop when you’re run down.
And the harm in just trying some?

This is the important bit. If your level is normal, extra testosterone won’t fix the tiredness. It tells your body to stop making its own, and that switches off sperm production. That can leave men infertile and with smaller testicles, sometimes for a long time. It also thickens the blood, which raises clot risk, and can cause acne, breast tissue growth and mood swings. Gym and online products aren’t regulated, so you can’t be sure what’s in them.
I didn’t know about the fertility thing.

So here’s my suggestion. Bloods this week: blood count, iron, thyroid, sugar, kidney and liver tests. A sleep questionnaire, and a mood questionnaire too, because feeling flat matters. Could you also try a lighter training block with proper rest days for a few weeks?
model.why: Proportionate work-up and a practical change

model.text: I can try that.

If your symptoms point more towards low testosterone as we go, I’ll arrange the two morning tests. If they are genuinely low, I’d involve a specialist rather than simply prescribing. And if you do ever decide to use gym products, please tell us first so we can check your blood and keep you safe.
model.why: Keeps testing conditional; offers harm reduction without endorsing use

model.text: If your mood drops a lot, or you have any thoughts of harming yourself, please contact us straight away. Otherwise, let’s review in two weeks with the results. What will you take away from today?
Bloods, sleep and mood checks, ease off training, and don’t just take the stuff because it could wreck my fertility.
That’s it exactly. See you in two weeks.

social.t: Body-image pressure and social media drive requests for testosterone. Engage with his goals and offer reliable information.
Men often present low mood as tiredness or loss of libido. Screen mood and ask about self-harm.

legal.t: Anabolic steroids are Class C controlled drugs (Misuse of Drugs Act 1971). Possession for personal use is not an offence, but supply is. Information he shares is confidential.
Prescribing testosterone without a confirmed indication falls short of GMC Good practice in prescribing and managing medicines and devices (2021).

professional.t: If he goes on to use products, offer non-judgemental support: bloods (FBC for haematocrit, lipids, liver function), blood pressure, and needle and syringe services (NICE PH52).
Confirmed testosterone deficiency in a young man needs a search for the cause and specialist advice (BSSM 2023).

community.t: Needle and syringe programmes and drug services increasingly support people using image- and performance-enhancing drugs. Talking therapies if low mood is confirmed.

redFlags: Weight loss, night sweats or other systemic symptoms
Low mood with hopelessness or self-harm thoughts
Headache or visual field change with suspected low testosterone (pituitary cause)
Current androgen use: polycythaemia, blood pressure, mood change
psychosocial: Training load and recovery, work stress
ice: Concern: going backwards despite training hard
Expectation: a test and a testosterone prescription

playbook.diagnosis: “Your tiredness is real, but in a man your age low testosterone is an uncommon cause. Sleep, mood, overtraining and common blood problems are more likely, so we check those first.”
playbook.diagnosisLay: “Testosterone works like a thermostat. If you add it from outside, your body turns its own supply down, including the part that makes sperm.”

management.reflectIce: “You’re putting the work in and feeling worse, so it makes sense you’d look for a quick fix. Let’s find out what’s really causing it.”
management.psychosocial: Agree a lighter training block with rest days, address sleep and alcohol, and check mood.
sharedPlan: Bloods: FBC, ferritin, TSH, HbA1c, renal and liver function
Epworth or STOP-Bang and a mood questionnaire
Two morning testosterone samples (7–11am) with LH, FSH, SHBG and prolactin only if symptoms suggest deficiency
Specialist route if deficiency is confirmed; no testosterone for tiredness
safetyNet: Contact the practice promptly if mood drops or thoughts of self-harm
Tell us before using any gym products so we can monitor safely

pitfalls.intro: This station tests whether you can decline a request without losing the patient. Examiners want a proper tiredness work-up, correct testing if needed, honest harm information, and a steroid question that gets an honest answer.

items.fail: Ordering a single random testosterone level.
items.why: Levels vary through the day and fall with illness; BSSM 2023 needs two morning samples with symptoms.
items.fix: Test only if symptoms suggest it, then two samples between 7 and 11am with LH, FSH, SHBG and prolactin.

items.fail: Jumping straight to testosterone without a tiredness history.
items.why: Misses sleep problems, depression, overtraining, anaemia, thyroid disease and diabetes.
items.fix: Screen sleep, mood, alcohol, training load and first-line bloods.

items.why: It is the harm young men least expect and the one most likely to change their decision.
items.fix: “It switches off sperm production and can leave men infertile.”

items.fail: Never asking about current steroid or SARM use.
items.why: Androgen use or withdrawal can cause these exact symptoms and needs harm reduction.
Dismissiveness loses him to unregulated sources.
items.fix: Acknowledge his goals and frustration, then explain.

items.why: “Flat” and poor sleep may be depression.
items.fix: Ask about mood and self-harm and give a clear route back.

items.why: He leaves with the problem unsolved and the products still available.
items.fix: Bloods, questionnaires, a training change, conditional testing and review in 2 weeks.

BSSM 2023 [1]: diagnosis needs consistent symptoms plus two morning total testosterone samples (7–11am, ideally fasting) on separate occasions, with LH and FSH to separate primary from secondary causes, and SHBG, prolactin and FBC. Acute illness lowers testosterone, so avoid testing when unwell.
In men with normal levels, testosterone does not treat tiredness. BSSM [1] reserves treatment for confirmed deficiency with symptoms, and it is not for men who want to preserve fertility.

points.h: Harms of testosterone and anabolic steroids
points.t: Exogenous androgens suppress LH and FSH, so the testes make less testosterone and fewer sperm: infertility and testicular shrinkage, which may be slow to recover. Also raised haematocrit (BSSM [1] monitoring threshold 54%), acne, gynaecomastia, mood change, adverse lipids and cardiovascular risk. Gym or online products are unregulated and may be contaminated.

Ask directly and without judgement about testosterone, anabolic steroids, SARMs or “boosters”. Stopping after a cycle can itself cause low mood, low libido and tiredness. NICE PH52 [4] includes people who inject image- and performance-enhancing drugs in needle and syringe programmes.

If two morning levels are low with symptoms, look for the cause (including prolactin and pituitary causes when LH is low or normal) and involve endocrinology or a specialist men’s health service before treatment.

SCA_SC_TASKS.d: Let him give the full story and the request; acknowledged the tiredness before discussing testosterone.
Training load and recovery, work and stress, sleep, alcohol, diet, gym culture and online influence.
Followed “flat”, poor sleep and “I’ve looked into it”; asked about steroids without judgement.
Idea (low testosterone), concern (going backwards despite effort), expectation (a test and a prescription).
FBC, ferritin, TSH, HbA1c, renal and liver function; Epworth/STOP-Bang; mood screen. Two morning testosterone samples (7–11am) with LH, FSH, SHBG and prolactin only if indicated.
Sleep problems, depression, overtraining, alcohol, anaemia, thyroid, diabetes, androgen use or withdrawal, true hypogonadism.
Asked about specific hypogonadism features, low mood and self-harm; recognised anabolic steroid use as a cause and a risk.
Explained that low testosterone is an unlikely cause and that the work-up comes first.
Declined to prescribe without confirmed deficiency; explained infertility and other harms; agreed a proportionate plan.
Training load, sleep, mood and alcohol addressed; specialist route for confirmed deficiency; harm reduction if he uses products.
Review in two weeks with results; mood safety-net; teach-back.

social.t: Body-image pressure and social media drive requests for testosterone. Engage with his goals and offer reliable information.
Men often present low mood as tiredness or loss of libido. Screen mood and ask about self-harm.

legal.t: Anabolic steroids are Class C controlled drugs (Misuse of Drugs Act 1971). Possession for personal use is not an offence, but supply is. Information he shares is confidential.
Prescribing testosterone without a confirmed indication falls short of GMC Good practice in prescribing and managing medicines and devices (2021).

professional.t: If he goes on to use products, offer non-judgemental support: bloods (FBC for haematocrit, lipids, liver function), blood pressure, and needle and syringe services (NICE PH52).
Confirmed testosterone deficiency in a young man needs a search for the cause and specialist advice (BSSM 2023).

community.t: Needle and syringe programmes and drug services increasingly support people using image- and performance-enhancing drugs. Talking therapies if low mood is confirmed.

redFlags: Weight loss, night sweats or other systemic symptoms
Low mood with hopelessness or self-harm thoughts
Headache or visual field change with suspected low testosterone (pituitary cause)
Current androgen use: polycythaemia, blood pressure, mood change
psychosocial: Training load and recovery, work stress
ice: Concern: going backwards despite training hard
Expectation: a test and a testosterone prescription

SCA_PLAYBOOK.diagnosis: “Your tiredness is real, but in a man your age low testosterone is an uncommon cause. Sleep, mood, overtraining and common blood problems are more likely, so we check those first.”
SCA_PLAYBOOK.diagnosisLay: “Testosterone works like a thermostat. If you add it from outside, your body turns its own supply down, including the part that makes sperm.”

management.reflectIce: “You’re putting the work in and feeling worse, so it makes sense you’d look for a quick fix. Let’s find out what’s really causing it.”
management.psychosocial: Agree a lighter training block with rest days, address sleep and alcohol, and check mood.

Two morning testosterone samples (7–11am) with LH, FSH, SHBG and prolactin only if symptoms suggest deficiency
Specialist route if deficiency is confirmed; no testosterone for tiredness

SCA_PITFALLS.intro: This station tests whether you can decline a request without losing the patient. Examiners want a proper tiredness work-up, correct testing if needed, honest harm information, and a steroid question that gets an honest answer.

items.fail: Ordering a single random testosterone level.
items.why: Levels vary through the day and fall with illness; BSSM 2023 needs two morning samples with symptoms.
items.fix: Test only if symptoms suggest it, then two samples between 7 and 11am with LH, FSH, SHBG and prolactin.

items.fail: Jumping straight to testosterone without a tiredness history.
items.why: Misses sleep problems, depression, overtraining, anaemia, thyroid disease and diabetes.
items.fix: Screen sleep, mood, alcohol, training load and first-line bloods.

items.why: It is the harm young men least expect and the one most likely to change their decision.
items.fix: “It switches off sperm production and can leave men infertile.”

items.fail: Never asking about current steroid or SARM use.
items.why: Androgen use or withdrawal can cause these exact symptoms and needs harm reduction.
Dismissiveness loses him to unregulated sources.
items.fix: Acknowledge his goals and frustration, then explain.

items.why: “Flat” and poor sleep may be depression.
items.fix: Ask about mood and self-harm and give a clear route back.

items.why: He leaves with the problem unsolved and the products still available.
items.fix: Bloods, questionnaires, a training change, conditional testing and review in 2 weeks.
